title: Tone curve module
objective: Deliver the Tone curve module: one composite point curve over encoded luminance, frozen against an independent reference, drawn by the delivered curve editor, programmable through edit.set-curve and query.sample-curve, maskable, presettable, and verified numerically, through the method table and on the M4 Mac.
context_summary: Planned on 2026-09-30 from docs/design/tone-curve.md; implementation is not yet authorized and the plan runs on the design's recorded proposal defaults. Everything the module needs exists: the field-patch module framework (modules/field_patch.rs), the `curve` parameter and control kinds with the point editor, channel switch and histogram background the developer controls proof exercises, the pointwise colour run and its masked blend, presets over every field-patch action, the field-patch conformance suite, and the frozen Basic tone vocabulary (encoded luminance, luminance-ratio reconstruction, near-black rule) in crates/luxforge-core/src/colour.rs. No new host primitive, control kind, stage or desktop message is expected; the plan verifies that on the real module and records any deviation. Decisions: docs/decisions.md.

tasks.description: Freeze the curve numerics: the f64 reference, its study, the oracle fixture and the design's measured figures.
extra_context: The interpolant is the design's open PCHIP: Fritsch-Butland weighted-harmonic-mean slopes at interior knots (zero when either adjacent secant is zero), secant end slopes, exactly constant segments between equal `y`, a flat hold inside [0, 1] beyond the point span, and a unit-slope tail outside [0, 1]. The mixer reference (crates/luxforge-reference/src/mixer.rs, `HueWarp`) holds the periodic form of the same construction; transcribe the open form into the new module rather than refactoring the mixer's frozen code, and keep its naming.

The reference takes and returns linear-sRGB f64 triples with no clamp, applying the curve to Rec. 709 luminance through the analytically continued sRGB encode and decode and the luminance-ratio reconstruction with the additive near-black rule, exactly as crates/luxforge-reference/src/tone.rs does; reuse that file's transfer functions and constants by name.

Named point sets for every property and comparison: the identity, a mid-tone lift, an S-curve, an inverse S, a lifted black, a cut white, a span inside [0.2, 0.8], a 16-point wiggle and a set with a flat pair; plus seeded random admissible lists (2 to 16 points, strictly increasing x, non-decreasing y) through the crate's SplitMix64.

Properties to prove: interpolation at every knot; non-decreasing forward differences on a 4001-point grid over [-0.5, 2.0] for every named set and at least 10,000 random lists; no overshoot (values within each segment's [y_i, y_{i+1}]); C1 continuity at interior knots; identity to within f64 rounding for on-diagonal points spanning [0, 1]; the two-point affine case; exact flat segments; finiteness over the extended domain; greys stay three bit-identical channels and Oklab hue is invariant under the reconstruction.

Comparison recorded in the design with numbers, not adjectives: on the same sets and grid, linear, natural cubic and Catmull-Rom interpolants against PCHIP for maximum overshoot beyond [0, 1], inversions, and the largest slope discontinuity at a knot; and on a 512-pixel 8-bit ramp, distinct codes and longest identical run per set, as docs/design/basic-tone.md's visual evidence did.

Freeze the tolerance at 1e-5 + 1e-5 * |reference| in linear float and one output code, and record the measured largest deviation once TASK-002 exists; until then the study records the reference's own round-trip figures.

Studies run as one binary filtered by module name: `cargo test -p luxforge-reference --test studies curve::`. The fixture is generated by an ignored test and reloaded on every ordinary run at 1e-12, as fixtures/mixer/README.md describes for the mixer.

tasks.description: Build the luxforge.curve field-patch module: descriptor, unit, sample query, registration and exactness against the frozen reference on both paths.
extra_context: A field-patch module is one `Spec` and a `compile` (crates/luxforge-core/src/modules/field_patch.rs); the vignette (modules/vignette/) and the mixer (modules/mixer/) are the templates, and the controls proof (modules/controls.rs) shows a curve field as a channel of a group's `extra` curve control and a `sample-*` query declared through `Spec::query`.

Descriptor: module `luxforge.curve`, title `Tone curve`, hint from the design; effect `luxforge.curve.tone` at the colour stage, order 5, maskable; field `luminance` of kind curve (2 to 16 points, monotone, no fixed x) with default [[0, 0], [1, 1]], step 0.01 and precision 2, history word `Tone curve`; one group `Tone curve` holding the field with the curve control (`sample-curve`, histogram background) as its extra; the section collapsed. The registry's `linked_modules` (modules/registry/mod.rs) lists it after Basic and before Presence.

Neutrality is the framework default (points equal the default). `compile` returns a colour operation with no units for the exact identity map (first point [0, 0], last [1, 1], every point on the diagonal) and otherwise exactly one `PointwiseColor` unit whose per-segment cubic coefficients, knot slopes and flat-hold values are computed in f64 and cast once to f32; `apply_row` ignores the row coordinates; `describe` writes every point with shortest round-trip floats; `is_finite` checks the cast coefficients.
The unit reuses `colour::srgb::{encode_f32, decode_f32}`, the luma helper and `colour::reconstruct` from crates/luxforge-core/src/colour.rs; it must not restate the transfer function.

`query.sample-curve` takes the one optional curve parameter without a default (what the descriptor validator requires of a sample query) and returns 257 [x, C(x)] samples at i/256 evaluated in f64 by the same construction the unit's coefficients come from.

Registering a built-in changes fixtures/modules/builtin-descriptors.json: regenerate it with the ignored snapshot test and review the diff; the developer-mode listing test must still add exactly the test modules' methods.

Answer the performance-rules checklist for this change under crates/: no new full-frame allocation, no point query that rasterizes, nothing new on the owner thread beyond the O(1) query, no new desktop message, timer or subscription.

tasks.description: Prove the module through the method table: the field-patch conformance suite and a Tone curve acceptance chapter for placement, masks and the sample query.
extra_context: The conformance suite (crates/luxforge-core/tests/modules/conformance/) finds field-patch modules from their descriptors and refuses to run when it no longer recognises the built-in ones: add `luxforge.curve` to its known list (conformance/mod.rs) so the module is checked in `cargo test` (the slow `field_patch` test) and in release inside `editor-acceptance`. Its shape rules already move a curve's points halfway toward a bound and count points past the maximum.

The chapter follows xtask/src/presence_mixer_vignette_acceptance.rs: driven through `OwnerHandle::call` as an independent client, one catalog per section under the run's output, recorded under `tone_curve` in result.json and listed in editor-acceptance's summary of what it proves.

Placement: commit the mixer then the curve, the curve then the mixer, and Basic last, and require the same bytes and the stored order Basic, curve, mixer in each case; a masked curve on two masks after the global one, in mask order, and re-sorted by `mask.reorder`.

Sample query: `query.sample-curve` for the displayed entry's points equals the compiled unit's curve (evaluated in f64 through the reference) at every one of the 257 samples to 1e-12, and the 8-bit output of a grey ramp rendered through the layer equals the quantized reference at every code.

tasks.description: Show the section in the desktop and capture native rendered evidence: the generated ramp fixture and the `curve` smoke scenario.
extra_context: No desktop change is expected: the section, the curve editor, the histogram background, the drag draft, add, remove, nudge, the point list, Original/Custom and the JSON-request menu are all generated from the descriptor (docs/design/ui-components.md). Verify that on the real module first; if a desktop change is needed, make it, record why in the design's module boundaries table and keep the widget crate pure.

Fixture: add `tone-ramp.jpg` to `generate-fixtures` (xtask/src/fixtures.rs, the table beside presence.jpg and range.jpg): a 512-wide encoded grey ramp band above a band of the four quadrant colours, deterministic, small, with its manifest entry; `verify` schedules generation when a listed fixture is missing.

Scenario (xtask/src/curve_smoke.rs, registered in xtask/src/smoke.rs like `mixer`): open with Basic collapsed and the section listed collapsed with no layer; expand; drag a mid-tone point through three positions with drafted frames and no commit; release and commit one entry labelled `Tone curve 3 points`; add a point; type an S-curve through the point list; module reset keeping the layer identity; a masked drag through a mask target. Verify on the frames: the grey ramp row has no decreasing step, its pixels stay grey, each quadrant's mean hue angle is unchanged, the S-curve lowers the lower half's mean and raises the upper half's, the longest identical run on the ramp stays within a stated bound of neutral's, and the curve editor is on screen with the histogram behind it; correlate every frame with `asset.state`, the draft and the events log.
Launch through the background bundle only; never run the GUI binary directly.

tasks.description: Carry the curve through presets: capture and apply of set-curve, and the Lightroom ToneCurvePV2012 transfer with the other curve rows re-worded.
extra_context: Every field-patch action is presettable through `ModuleRegistry::patch_action`, so `set-curve` joins settings sets, capture, apply, the create form's groups and export with no core change; prove it rather than assume it, on a JPEG and a RAW photo.

Lightroom mapping (crates/luxforge-core/src/presets/mapping.rs): `ToneCurvePV2012` becomes a new rule kind that transfers an `rdf:Seq` of `"x, y"` items on the 0-255 scale onto `set-curve.luminance` as [x/255, y/255] pairs, refused with its reason for more than sixteen or fewer than two points, a non-increasing x or a decreasing y, never decimated, clamped or reordered, and neutral for an identity list (presets/value.rs already recognises one); `ToneCurveName2012` neutral; the Red, Green and Blue curves unsupported with the reason `Luxforge's tone curve has no per-channel curves`; the parametric fields unsupported with `Luxforge has no parametric curve`; the `EnableToneCurve` panel switch as delivered. The mapping test that every mapped target is a registered presettable parameter covers the new row.

tasks.description: Measure the module on photo-sized inputs, record the figures, update the documentation and hand off with the rendered tier.
extra_context: Timing waits until the feature is complete, as the performance rules require. `editor-latency --control curve` drives the developer proof's curve today; extend it to drive a named module's curve (an `--action set-curve --parameter luminance` form for a curve kind, or a module flag) so the Tone curve's point drag is measured with the same strict request-to-frame correlation, at 24 MP and 60 MP with 30 inputs, against the slider budget (16 ms p95, acceptable below 32 ms, warm 24 MP at Fit) and the settled histogram budget (200 ms p95). Record the one-minute load with each figure through the shared reliability rule.

Measure the unit's own frame cost with `editor-performance` (add a curve recipe beside the Basic ones, or a core timing test in the style of the kernel table) at 24 MP and 60 MP, 30 samples, and compare with the composed Tone stages' recorded 48 and 127 ms; record p50/p95, host, profile and cache state in docs/specs/performance.md.

Documentation for demonstrated behaviour only: docs/features.md (a Tone curve row), docs/user-guide.md (a Tone curve section after Basic, the sentence that Tone Curve is not a photo tool yet, and the import list), docs/design/develop-workspace.md (the tool array row), docs/design/modules-and-api.md (the registry order, the descriptor paragraph and the conformance module list), docs/design/architecture.md (the reference and built-in module lists), docs/decisions.md (the curve vocabulary's consumer under UI components), docs/design/tone-curve.md (status implemented and verified, measured figures, any deviation), and docs/plan.md.
A miss against a provisional budget is reported with its figures and does not block the handoff; no cache, table or timer is added to claim a pass.
